newsitem.title: UK: Speculative funds drive a sell-off in coffee.
newsitem.headline: Speculative funds drive a sell-off in coffee.

text.p: Coffee markets were jolted on Tuesday by a sell-off by speculative funds, taking London futures prices for the robusta type of beans to their lowest levels in 11 weeks.
A mass bale-out in coffee followed a five-month rally on tight supply that had lifted the market to 20-months highs in late May at $2,700. But since then prices have been drifting lower.
Tuesday morning saw London September robusta coffee futures drop more than 5.8 percent to $1,635 per tonne, the lowest since late April, as funds liquidated their long positions built over the rally.
By 1418 GMT, London's September futures had fallen even further, losing $125 at a session low of $1,610, a 7.2 percent fall.
The slide, aided by Asian producer selling, accelerated in the afternoon after a similar fall on the New York futures for the premium arabica types.
"It's all fund selling and there's no buying around," said one floor trader.

The September contract had earlier slipped through the previous major support at $1,695. This triggered sell stops and long liquidation by funds and speculators. The next key support was pegged at the triple bottom of around $1,610. Volume was brisk at about 10,000 lots.
Traders were unable to pinpoint specific fundamental reasons behind the sharp falls.
The winter in Brazil remained mild, with no frost forecast through July 22, while coffee stocks in the United States were building up again.

Analysts said the seasonal consumption dip during northern hemisphere summer and the impact of recent retail price increases that followed the rally earlier in the year helped put a lid on new buying by roasters (processors).
